name: FSMA Part 9 — Digital Token Service Provider (DTSP) framework
reference: Financial Services and Markets Act 2022 (FSMA), Part 9

articles.title: DTSP scope — outbound-only digital token services
articles.requirement: A person carrying on a business of providing one or more digital token services, where the person is incorporated / formed / based in Singapore + provides the service solely to persons outside Singapore, is a DTSP. Closes a previously deliberate scope gap: the PSA covers DPT service providers serving Singapore customers; the SFA covers capital-markets DPTs; outbound-only Singapore-domiciled providers previously fell between both Acts.

articles.title: Digital token service — definition
articles.requirement: Means any of: (a) dealing in digital tokens; (b) facilitating the exchange of digital tokens; (c) accepting custody, control or possession of digital tokens belonging to another person; (d) facilitating the transmission of digital tokens; (e) inducing or attempting to induce any person to enter into a digital token transaction; (f) facilitating + carrying out any other activity that may from time to time be prescribed.

articles.title: Licensing requirement
articles.requirement: No person may carry on a business of providing any digital token service in scope of §136 unless granted a licence by MAS under §139. MAS may refuse a licence on broad grounds incl. concerns about money-laundering risk, terrorism-financing risk, proliferation-financing risk, operational soundness, or the suitability of directors / key officers / substantial shareholders. The approval bar is deliberately narrow.

articles.title: Fit + proper requirements
articles.requirement: Applicant must satisfy fit + proper criteria for: directors, key officers (incl. CEO, AML compliance officer, technology risk officer), substantial shareholders + controllers. Standard MAS fit-and-proper criteria: integrity, competence, financial soundness. Applicant must also demonstrate adequate AML/CFT/PF systems, technology-risk framework, capital adequacy, sound business plan.

articles.title: Capital + financial soundness
articles.requirement: Minimum capital requirements prescribed by MAS Notice — similar to PSA MPI/SPI structure proportionate to business scale + risk profile. Ongoing financial-soundness reporting + capital adequacy maintenance required.

articles.title: AML/CFT obligations — MAS Notice PSN01-equivalent
articles.requirement: DTSP licensees subject to AML/CFT/PF obligations equivalent to those imposed on PSA DPT service providers (i.e. MAS Notice PSN02 structure, aligned with MAS Notice 626). Includes: entity-wide risk assessment with PF dimension; CDD; EDD for high-risk; PEPs; STR to STRO; sanctions screening + targeted financial measures; tipping-off prohibition; internal policies + training + record retention.

articles.title: Technology risk management
articles.requirement: DTSP licensees must implement technology-risk management aligned with MAS TRM Guidelines proportionate to scale + risk: technology-risk governance; security controls; cybersecurity (incl. wallet + key management); IT-incident management + reporting to MAS; cloud + IT third-party management. Particular emphasis on private-key custody + wallet-security given the bearer-instrument nature of digital tokens.

articles.title: Custody + safeguarding of customer digital tokens
articles.requirement: Where DTSP holds custody of customer digital tokens: customer-asset segregation (separation of customer DT from own holdings); insolvency-remote arrangements; secure custody (cold + hot wallet structure proportionate to risk; key-management framework; multi-party computation or HSM-style controls); reporting customer-asset balances to MAS on prescribed cadence; independent assurance over custody arrangements.

articles.title: Conduct + business obligations
articles.requirement: DTSP licensees subject to MAS conduct expectations: fit-and-proper customer onboarding; clear + fair customer communications; suitability + appropriateness where advisory services provided; complaint-handling; protection of customer assets. Where the DTSP also conducts PSA DPT services for Singapore customers, the more onerous of the two regimes applies.

articles.title: Enforcement powers
articles.requirement: MAS enforcement powers under Part 9 include: civil + criminal sanctions for unlicensed operation; licence suspension or revocation for breaches; civil monetary penalties for AML/CFT failures; prohibition orders against individuals; remediation orders. Criminal offence carries up to 3 years' imprisonment + S$250,000 fine for individuals or S$500,000 for bodies corporate for unlicensed operation.

articles.title: Transition + exit for outbound-only DTSPs
articles.requirement: Persons that were providing in-scope outbound-only DT services prior to 30 June 2025 had to either apply for a DTSP licence by the deadline OR cease the in-scope activities by 30 June 2025. Many established Singapore-based outbound-only DT entities chose to exit Singapore (relocating to Hong Kong, UAE, or other crypto-permissive jurisdictions) rather than face the narrow approval bar. MAS has issued few DTSP licences in the first 6 months of the regime.
